summary: Exposed lightstation on Robb Point, Milbanke Sound, B.C.: lit 1 October 1898; keepers' house flooded in a 1982 Christmas storm; still staffed.

structures.note: Red steel tower from 1957 (LF, Lighthouse Digest); the CCG list gives a skeleton tower 26.0 m

access.note: Staffed Coast Guard lightstation: keepers' home and workplace. Visit only where the station welcomes visitors; never land uninvited. Lighthouse Friends: grounds open, tower closed.

visit.note: Best seen from the water; visible from ferries serving the Inside Passage out of Port Hardy (LF)

events.note: Put in operation 1 October 1898, the building erected by day labour under Alexander Bruce of Vancouver
Fog-alarm building completed and 1 1/2-inch diaphone installed (report year ended 31 March 1908)
Fog-alarm building damaged by sea after an earthquake tidal wave (December 1908)
Breakwater built and tower raised so the fog alarm would not obscure the light (summer 1909)
Landing boat capsized in surf; deckhand John Desmuelles drowned, two men rescued
Tidal wave in November 1941 damaged the bridge to the lighthouse point
Light on the square dwelling replaced by a red steel tower
Christmas 1982 gale; wave flooded the station; only the dwelling and radio antenna left standing

corrections.why: Lighthouse Friends and Lighthouse Digest's earlier-towers list both date the red steel tower to 1957. Lighthouse Digest's 2006 entry also gives 'Date Present Tower Built: 1983', so a 1983 date does appear in a cited source, but it conflicts with the same entry's 1957 steel tower and with Lighthouse Friends, which gives no later tower. The 1983 date is not confirmed; review before applying.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's conflict asks whether the light is still lit. Lighthouse Friends says the station remains staffed with keepers listed to 2024, and the Coast Guard list gives an active Fl W 5s light. The DFO Shore Station series ended in 1955 ('archived') because the sampling stopped, not because the light was discontinued.
Lighthouse Friends gives 66 ft (20.1 m) for the 1898 light; the Coast Guard list gives 20.5 m for the present light. The figures are for different structures and do not contradict.
Coast Guard list gives 26.0 m for the skeleton tower; Lighthouse Digest's 2006 entry gives tower height 17 without a unit. The Digest figure is not used.

Lighthouse Digest (2006) lists a 1957 steel tower under earlier towers and 'Date Present Tower Built: 1983'; Lighthouse Friends gives 1957 for the red steel tower and no later tower. The story states the 1957 tower and the Digest's 1983 date and does not choose between them.

Lighthouse Digest (2006): wooden keeper's house 'destroyed by storm in December 1982'. Lighthouse Friends: after the storm only the dwelling and radio antenna were standing, and the original square dwelling was still at the station in 2010. Both are stated in the story.
Coast Guard list: 16 nautical miles (used in the story). Lighthouse Digest (2006): 15 nautical miles, which the story also gives.

notes_for_editor: Keeper names and years are Lighthouse Friends' head-keeper list. Reuter's 2 May 1905 appointment (1909 keepers' table, scan 179, printed 172) was matched by column position in the OCR; the same date appears in the 1910 volume's table (scan 179, 'F. Reuter : May 2, 1905') and in the 1906 list, where 'Reuter, F Ivory Island' sits beside a jumbled 'May ... 2, 1905'; the 1907 list (scan 156) puts Reuter at Ivory Island. The page image could not be opened from the review session, so the column match rests on OCR. The 1898 description of the lighthouse (first light, 1 October 1898 operation, 66 ft focal height) is from Lighthouse Friends quoting the Department of Marine notice, which is not in the local corpus; the story says so. The 1942 Findlay article is read through Lighthouse Friends, which cites The Vancouver Sun; the story does not cite the newspaper directly, and does not give a year for the 1941 tidal wave. The DFO CSV marks the Ivory series 'archived' and calls it a 'random site' in a short time series; the open-data page says eleven stations were added in the mid-1930s but does not name Ivory, so the story no longer says Ivory was part of that programme. Lighthouse Digest (2006) disagrees with Lighthouse Friends on the present tower date (1983), the wooden keeper's house (destroyed December 1982), and range (15 nm); all three are stated in the story. The record's 1983 correction is revised (see corrections). Nauticapedia refused access (403) and was not used. The 32-foot figure is converted to 9.8 m. Post-1960 keepers are named only as Lighthouse Friends prints them; Gordon Schweers appears in his published public role.
